docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example DAIV_SANDBOX_URL URL of the sandbox service http://sandbox:8000 http://sandbox:8000 DAIV_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT Timeout for sandbox requests in seconds, and the longest timeout the agent can give a bash command, whose request waits up to 60 seconds longer 600 600 DAIV_SANDBOX_API_KEY API key for sandbox requests (none) random-api-key DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_DISALLOW JSON array of extra bash command rules to block globally (none) '["curl", "npm publish"]' DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_ALLOW JSON array of bash command rules to permit; has no effect (see Precedence) (none) '["my-safe-tool"]'

Both command policy settings take a JSON array. A plain string such as curl wget, or an empty value, fails to parse and DAIV does not start. The outer single quotes in the examples are YAML or shell quoting, not part of the value. For how entries are matched and which rules are built in, see Sandbox.

The sandbox service has its own settings; see Deployment files and the daiv-sandbox repository.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
DAIV uses django-allauth for web authentication. Users sign in with a Git platform account (GitHub or GitLab) or with a passwordless login code sent by email. Email signup is off. For how accounts are created, see Accounts and roles, and for who becomes the first admin, the section of that page.

The OAuth variables below override the matching fields of the Authentication group of Site Configuration and lock them; the group also holds an Enable OAuth login toggle. To create the OAuth app that gives you the client ID and secret, see Create the OAuth app.

Variable Description Default Example DAIV_AUTH_LOGIN_ENABLED Show the social provider button on the login page false true DAIV_AUTH_SIGNUP_OPEN Allow anyone authenticating via the configured Git platform to self-create an account. When off, only admin-pre-created users can sign in false true ALLAUTH_CLIENT_ID OAuth client ID for the configured Git platform (none) Iv1.abc123 ALLAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET OAuth client secret for the configured Git platform (none) ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL GitLab instance URL (for OAuth redirects to the user's browser) https://gitlab.com https://gitlab.example.com ALLAUTH_GITLAB_SERVER_URL GitLab server URL (for server-to-server API calls, if different from ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL) (none) http://gitlab:8929 EMAIL_BACKEND Django email backend for login-by-code emails django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend EMAIL_HOST SMTP server hostname localhost smtp.example.com EMAIL_PORT SMTP server port 25 587 EMAIL_HOST_USER SMTP authentication username (empty) user@example.com EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD SMTP authentication password (empty) EMAIL_USE_TLS Use TLS for SMTP connection False True DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL Sender address for login-by-code emails noreply@daiv.dev noreply@example.com

OAuth login needs all three of the DAIV_AUTH_LOGIN_ENABLED toggle, a client ID and a client secret. If you set only one of the client ID and the secret, DAIV logs a warning and does not show the provider button on the login page. The CODEBASE_CLIENT setting decides which provider, GitHub or GitLab, DAIV offers.

With EMAIL_BACKEND set to django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend, DAIV writes login-code emails to the app's output instead of sending them, which is enough to sign in without an SMTP server.

docs.text:

Two more variables exist, but leave them unset: each pins a value that DAIV otherwise derives.

(derived) daiv_bot DAIV_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET Pins the webhook secret. It must not be empty: a blank value makes the webhook reject every update. (generated)

docs.title: External URL and encryption key
docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL External URL of the application. https://127.0.0.1:8000 https://daiv.example.com DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY Fernet encryption key for secrets stored in the database. If not set, a key is derived from DJANGO_SECRET_KEY via HKDF. (derived)

DAIV uses DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL to define webhooks on the Git platform and as the site domain in authentication emails, so the Git platform must be able to reach it.

DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY protects the secrets DAIV stores in its database: provider API keys, the Tavily web search API key, the OAuth client secret, the sandbox API key, the Rocket.Chat token, the Telegram bot token and webhook secret, web fetch header values, MCP server headers, and sandbox environment variables and egress secrets. DAIV uses a raw Fernet key directly. Any other value is a passphrase, from which DAIV derives a key with HKDF-SHA256. When the variable is unset, DAIV derives the key from DJANGO_SECRET_KEY.

Warning

Back up DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY, or DJANGO_SECRET_KEY when you leave it unset. If the key is lost or changed, DAIV cannot decrypt the stored secrets, and you must enter them again.

docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example DAIV_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID Umami website ID. When set, the public homepage and /compare/ pages load Umami's tracker for signed-out visitors. (none) 0b6bd0c4-5d6c-4f2e-9a43-1d2e3f4a5b6c DAIV_UMAMI_SCRIPT_URL URL of Umami's tracker script; set it to use a self-hosted Umami. https://cloud.umami.is/script.js https://stats.example.com/script.js

Analytics is off unless you set DAIV_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID, so DAIV sends no visitor data by default. When it is set, the tracker uses no cookies, honours the browser's Do Not Track setting, and never loads for signed-in users or on dashboard pages.

docs.title: Git platform
docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example CODEBASE_CLIENT Client to use for codebase operations gitlab gitlab or github CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON Cron expression for periodic webhook setup (GitLab only) */5 * * * * */10 * * * * CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_SYNC_CRON Cron expression for the periodic repository access sync */15 * * * * */10 * * * * CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_HARD_TTL_HOURS Hours a repository's synced access data stays trusted before it is denied (fails closed); tracked per repository 24 12

Set CODEBASE_CLIENT to gitlab or github. Only one platform is active at a time.

CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_SYNC_CRON sets how often DAIV copies each user's repository membership from the Git platform into its database, with one member-list call per repository. Admins are exempt from repository authorization and always have full access. DAIV tracks freshness per repository: if a repository's sync stops succeeding, for example because the platform token loses access to it, DAIV keeps using the last known access data until CODEBASE_REPO_ACCESS_HARD_TTL_HOURS elapse. After that the repository denies access, while the others keep syncing. See Accounts and roles for the access model.

docs.title: GitLab
docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example CODEBASE_GITLAB_URL URL of the GitLab instance (none) https://gitlab.com CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN Authentication token for GitLab (none) glpat-xyz CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET Secret token for GitLab webhook validation. Without it, every GitLab webhook request is rejected with 401 (none) random-webhook-secret

CODEBASE_GITLAB_AUTH_TOKEN is a personal access token with the api scope.

For git clone and git push, DAIV does not put this token in the repository workspace. It creates a short-lived project access token for each repository instead: named daiv-clone, with the write_repository scope and the Developer access level, and valid for 48 to 72 hours. DAIV reuses a repository's token for up to 24 hours, so expect a few daiv-clone bot members on a project at a time. GitLab removes expired ones.

Creating these tokens needs the token's user to hold at least the Maintainer role on each project and, on GitLab.com, the Premium or Ultimate tier. Self-managed instances accept any tier. When DAIV cannot create a token, it logs a warning and falls back to the personal access token.

The project access token pushes at the Developer level. If a branch protection rule matches the branches DAIV pushes to, for example a wildcard pattern that limits pushes to Maintainers, allow Developers to push on that pattern, or pushes fail.

Warning

Revoking a daiv-clone token early makes the next clone of that project fail authentication until DAIV drops the cached token and creates a new one, which happens after about 15 seconds of retries. The cache entry is codebase:gitlab:clone-token:<project-id>.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
Variable Description Default Example CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL URL of the GitHub instance (none) https://github.com CODEBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID GitHub App ID (none) 123456 CODEBASE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID GitHub App Installation ID (none) 789012 CODEBASE_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY GitHub App private key (PEM format) (none) CODEBASE_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET Secret token for GitHub webhook validation. Without it, every GitHub webhook request is rejected with 401 (none) random-webhook-secret

GitHub uses GitHub App authentication, so you create a GitHub App in your account or organization settings. The private key is a multi-line PEM file; store it as a Docker secret. For GitHub Enterprise Server, set CODEBASE_GITHUB_URL to its URL, for example https://github.example.com. For GitHub.com, you can omit it.

docs.title: LLM providers
docs.text:
Configure at least one provider to use the agent. The LLM providers page explains how model specs pick a provider.

Provider keys are seed-only

DAIV reads the provider API key variables once, when it first creates the provider records, and never again. They are not part of the environment, database and default order that other settings follow. Changing or adding a *_API_KEY variable or secret after the provider record exists has no effect: edit the provider under Configuration → Providers instead, which holds the key and the base URL from then on. A provider created without a key starts disabled.

DAIV reads each key from a Docker secret named after the variable in lowercase, for example openrouter_api_key mounted at /run/secrets/openrouter_api_key, or else from the environment variable. The secret wins when both are set. The OpenRouter base URL is a Base URL field of the provider and defaults to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. Providers describes the fields.

docs.text:
The native web_fetch tool fetches a URL, converts HTML to markdown, and has a small model answer a prompt about the page. A #fragment on an HTML page's URL limits it to the section that anchor names. A page over the maximum content size is rejected with a list of its section anchors.

When set, it replaces the Per-domain auth headers rows of the Web Fetch group, which then show a lock badge {} {"example.com": {"X-API-Key": "sk-abc"}}

docs.text:

Variable Description Default Example DAIV_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES Maximum size of one published file, in bytes (at most 64 MiB, the sandbox download limit) 10485760 (10 MiB) 52428800 DAIV_ARTIFACTS_PER_RUN_MAX Maximum number of files one run may publish 20 50 DAIV_TOOL_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES Maximum size of one image or file kept from a tool result for the transcript, in bytes 10485760 (10 MiB) 20971520 DAIV_TOOL_MEDIA_PER_RUN_MAX Maximum number of images and files kept from one run's tool results 100 200

docs.text: Variable Description Default Example DAIV_SHOW_RAW_TOOL_DATA Show each tool call's raw arguments and result in a closed Raw section of the call's details in the session transcript (env-only) (follows DJANGO_DEBUG) true

docs.title: MCP tools
docs.text:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools give the agent access to external services. DAIV stores MCP servers as database rows, which you manage at /dashboard/mcp-servers/, and connects to them directly, with no sidecar containers. For user-defined servers, see MCP tools.

Variable Description Default Example MCP_TOOL_LOAD_TIMEOUT Max seconds to wait for a single MCP server to return its tools before skipping it (keeps a broken/slow server from freezing chats and runs) 30 10

docs.title: Deferred tools
docs.text:
With deferred tools on, DAIV loads tools outside the always-loaded set on demand through a tool_search tool, instead of binding them to the model up front. Most deployments do not need to change these variables.

Variable Description Default Example DEFERRED_TOOLS_ENABLED Defer non-essential tools behind tool_search instead of binding them eagerly true false DEFERRED_TOOLS_TOP_K_DEFAULT Default number of results returned by a tool_search call 3 5 DEFERRED_TOOLS_TOP_K_MAX Maximum number of results tool_search will return per call 10 20 DEFERRED_TOOLS_FROZEN_TOOLS_MODELS Prefix-matched model names whose bound tools array is kept frozen (loaded schemas reach them via tool_search results only), preserving the provider prompt cache. Empty list disables freezing. claude-,anthropic/claude-,qwen/qwen3.8-max,minimax/minimax-m3,google/gemini-3.7-flash claude- DEFERRED_TOOLS_INLINE_TOOLS_MODELS Prefix-matched model names that get each loaded tool declared mid-conversation, right after the tool_search result that loaded it, through the provider's native mechanism (Anthropic tool_addition, OpenAI Responses additional_tools). The tools array stays frozen, so loading a tool keeps the prompt cache, and the model calls a declared tool. Applies only to models reached through the Anthropic API, or through an OpenAI-typed provider over the Responses API (the provider's Responses API setting is on, or the model is GPT 6, which langchain-openai sends there whenever tools are bound); on the Anthropic API, only to models langchain-anthropic keeps mid-conversation system messages in place for (not Claude Sonnet 5 or Haiku 5.5, for example). Empty list disables it. claude-,gpt-6-sol,gpt-6-luna,gpt-5.6-luna claude-opus-5 DEFERRED_TOOLS_EMBED_SCHEMAS_IN_RESULTS Embed each loaded tool's full schema in the tool_search result. Emergency valve: when false, results carry summaries only and freezing and inline definitions are forced off, so every model falls back to the array-append + summary pre-change behaviour. true false

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Learns from finished runs, consolidates what they teach into a per-repository document, and injects it into future runs.

Variable Description Default DAIV_MEMORY_ENABLED Capture learnings from finished runs, consolidate them, and inject them into future runs. A per-repository .daiv.yml flag can still opt an individual repository out true DAIV_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_MODEL_NAME Cheap model that extracts candidate observations from each finished run's transcript openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna DAIV_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME Fallback model when the extraction model fails openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL_NAME Model that rewrites the memory document. Leave empty to reuse the repository's agent model (none) DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MIN_PENDING Consolidate once at least this many pending observations have accumulated (subject to the consolidation interval below) 10 DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_PENDING_AGE_DAYS Consolidate a repository that is still below the threshold above once its oldest pending observation reaches this age, so low-volume repositories still form memory 7 DAIV_MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS Minimum hours between consolidations for the same repository 24 DAIV_MEMORY_MAX_LINES Cap on the memory document length in lines; entries beyond it are evicted 200 DAIV_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES Cap on the memory document size in bytes; entries beyond it are evicted 10240

docs.title: Run classifier
docs.text:
Classifies the report of each finished scheduled run into an envelope.

Variable Description Default DAIV_RUN_CLASSIFIER_MODEL_NAME Model that classifies each finished scheduled run's report into an envelope openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna DAIV_RUN_CLASSIFIER_FALLBACK_MODEL_NAME Fallback model when the classifier model fails openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

docs.title: Pipeline watch
docs.text:
Watches the CI of merge requests DAIV publishes and spends a bounded number of agent runs fixing failures; see Pipeline watch.

Variable Description Default DAIV_PIPELINE_WATCH_ENABLED Watch CI on merge requests DAIV publishes and try to fix failures true DAIV_PIPELINE_WATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS How many fix attempts to spend on one merge request before handing back (at least 1) 3

docs.title: Deployment files
docs.text:
The sample deployment files set the variables below. The DAIV_SANDBOX_* variables configure the daiv-sandbox container, not the DAIV app, and Docker reads DAIV_IMAGE_TAG when it starts the stack.

Variable Read by Description Default Example DAIV_SANDBOX_REDIS_URL Sandbox service Redis URL for per-session locking and for removing running sessions that stop receiving requests. Without it, the sandbox disables both and logs a warning (none) redis://redis:6379/3 DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_CERT_FILE Sandbox service Path to the egress CA certificate that the sandbox's egress proxy signs with. Set it together with the key file: the sandbox does not start with only one (none) /run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_cert DAIV_SANDBOX_EGRESS_CA_KEY_FILE Sandbox service Path to the egress CA private key. Without both files, the sandbox rejects sessions that need the egress proxy and the run fails (none) /run/secrets/daiv_sandbox_egress_ca_key DAIV_IMAGE_TAG Docker Tag of the DAIV image that the sample services pull; pin it to roll back to a build main sha-5e4f0d0

To create the egress CA and store it as secrets, see Deployment.

docs.title: Management commands
docs.text:
DAIV ships twelve django-admin commands for setup and operator repairs. Run them inside the app container:

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin <command>

Four of the twelve run on their own, so a manual run is the exception:

Command Runs on its own setup_default_site On every container start setup_checkpoint_saver On every container start sync_stuck_runs Every 5 minutes setup_webhooks On the CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON schedule, on GitLab only

The other eight run only when you run them.

docs.title: archive_sessions
docs.text:
Copies the live checkpoint of every session that has no archive into the session archive, so the transcript outlives the checkpointer TTL. Run it once after upgrading to the release that archives sessions, before those checkpoints expire; the upgrade note of that release in CHANGELOG.md says so. Running it again retries the sessions that failed. It does not run on its own.

This command takes no options.

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin archive_sessions

docs.title: backfill_memory_entries
docs.text:
Rebuilds a repository's memory entries by replaying its historical consolidated observations through the consolidation operations pass, oldest first. It makes LLM calls. Running it again replays only the observations that no entry covers. It ignores the memory enabled flags, because it is an operator repair action. It does not run on its own.

Warning

--reset-document clears the repository's stored memory document before replaying. DAIV keeps the old text only in a WARNING log line, so copy it from the command's output or your log pipeline if you may need it.

Option Description --repo-id Repository ID to backfill, for example group/project. Required. --batch-size Observations per operations round, from 1 to 50. Default: 20. --reset-document Clear the stored memory document before replaying. Use it for a repository whose document no replay can reconstruct. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin backfill_memory_entries --repo-id group/project

docs.title: bootstrap_admin
docs.text:
Creates the initial admin user when no admin exists yet. The command refuses to run if an admin exists, or if a user with that email exists. The new admin signs in with a one-time code sent by email; see Deployment. It does not run on its own.

Argument Description email Email address of the new admin user. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin bootstrap_admin admin@example.com

docs.title: consolidate_memory
docs.text:
Consolidates the pending memory observations of one repository into its memory document, in the foreground. The shell waits for the consolidation model's LLM call, and the call is billed like any other. DAIV's own hourly sweep does not use this command; it enqueues consolidation for the repositories that are due. This command does not run on its own.

Without --force, the command refuses to run while fewer than 10 observations are pending.

Option Description --repo-id Repository ID to consolidate, for example group/project. Required. --force Consolidate even below the pending-observation threshold. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin consolidate_memory --repo-id group/project

docs.title: create_api_key
docs.text:
Creates an API key for a user, for the Jobs API and other API clients. The key is printed once, on creation. It does not run on its own.

A time in --expires-at without an offset is read in Europe/Lisbon, not in the zone of your server or shell; see Time zone. Give an explicit offset to avoid the ambiguity.

Argument / option Description username Username of the user to create the key for. --name Name of the key. Default: empty. --expires-at Expiry in ISO 8601 format, for example 2026-12-31T23:59:59+00:00. Default: the key does not expire. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin create_api_key <username> --name "my-key" --expires-at 2026-12-31T23:59:59+00:00

Replace <username> with the username of the key's owner.

docs.title: export_session_archives
docs.text:
Writes each archived session's contexts and runs to <output>/<thread_id>.json, for offline analysis. See Export session archives for what an export holds. It does not run on its own.

The exports hold full conversations and run prompts. Inside the app container, a relative output resolves in the container, so the files never reach the host on their own. Write them to a temporary directory, copy them out, and delete the directory in the container.

Argument / option Description output Directory to write the files to. DAIV creates it if missing. --since Only sessions active on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD. --repo Only sessions on this repository, for example group/project. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin export_session_archives /tmp/session-exports --since 2026-10-01 --repo group/project
docker compose cp app:/tmp/session-exports ./session-exports
docker compose exec app rm -rf /tmp/session-exports

docs.title: release_orphan_queued_sessions
docs.text:
Releases queued runs whose session has no active sibling (a ready or running run). It mitigates a rare race where the dispatcher missed a terminal transition, or a run was created queued and never picked up; a sessions log message points here when that happens. It does not run on its own.

This command takes no options.

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin release_orphan_queued_sessions

docs.title: setup_checkpoint_saver
docs.text:
Initializes the LangGraph Redis checkpointer indices. It runs on every container start, so run it by hand only after you reset the checkpointer's Redis store while DAIV is running.

This command takes no options.

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_checkpoint_saver

docs.title: setup_default_site
docs.text:
Updates the default Django Site domain from DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL, so sign-in emails link to the right host. It runs on every container start; run it by hand after you change DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL without restarting.

This command takes no options.

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_default_site

docs.title: setup_langsmith_dashboard
docs.text:
Creates the LangSmith custom dashboard DAIV Monitoring, with the monitoring charts for DAIV. See Create the LangSmith dashboard. It needs LANGSMITH_API_KEY set in the container. It does not run on its own.

Warning

--recreate deletes the existing DAIV Monitoring dashboard, including any chart you added to it by hand, and creates it again.

Option Description --project LangSmith project name. Default: the LANGCHAIN_PROJECT environment variable, then LANGSMITH_PROJECT, then default. --recreate Delete the existing dashboard and create it again. Without it, the command fails when the dashboard exists. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_langsmith_dashboard --project <project-name>

Replace <project-name> with your LangSmith project.

docs.title: setup_webhooks
docs.text:
Sets the DAIV webhook on every repository DAIV can access, so issue and merge request events reach the instance.

This command is GitLab only. GitHub webhooks are set in the GitHub App's configuration, so on GitHub the command logs a warning and returns; see Platform setup. On GitLab it also runs on its own on the CODEBASE_WEBHOOK_SETUP_CRON schedule, so run it by hand only to add webhooks right away, or with --update to change the existing ones.

Warning

--disable-ssl-verification makes GitLab post webhook payloads, with the secret token in the X-Gitlab-Token header, without checking DAIV's certificate. Use it for local setups with self-signed certificates only. The scheduled run sets it only when DEBUG is on.

Warning

A token passed with --secret-token lands in your shell history and shows in the process list while the command runs. Set CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET instead, and keep the flag for one-off overrides.

Option Description --base-url Base URL of DAIV. Default: DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL. --repo-id Only set up this repository ID. --secret-token Secret token for webhook validation. Overrides CODEBASE_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. --disable-ssl-verification Tell GitLab not to verify DAIV's SSL certificate for the webhook. --update Update existing webhooks as well as creating missing ones. Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin setup_webhooks --update

docs.title: sync_stuck_runs
docs.text:
Reconciles runs that are not in a terminal state:

  • Task-backed runs are re-synced from their linked task result.
  • Inline chat runs that a worker crash left running are failed once their session heartbeat goes stale. Task-backed job and inbox runs in the same state are failed the same way.
  • Ready runs whose submitter stopped before queueing their task are failed once they are old enough.

It runs on its own every 5 minutes, so run it by hand only to reconcile right away.

This command takes no options.

Bash
docker compose exec app django-admin sync_stuck_runs

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: DAIV reports on its agent runs in two places. LangSmith holds the trace of each run: latency, tool calls and intermediate steps. DAIV's own database holds each run's token usage and estimated cost, and a copy of each session's conversation. This page covers both, and the log events DAIV writes when something needs an operator.

docs.title: Trace runs with LangSmith
docs.text:
DAIV sends a trace of every agent run to LangSmith once you set three variables. You need a LangSmith account.

  1. In LangSmith, select Settings → API Keys → Create API Key.
  2. Copy the key.

  3. Set LANGSMITH_TRACING to true, LANGSMITH_PROJECT to the project to write traces to, and LANGSMITH_API_KEY to the key. Monitoring (LangSmith) describes each variable, including the Docker secret form of the key and the EU endpoint.

    YAML
    x-app-defaults: &x_app_default
  environment:
    LANGSMITH_TRACING: true
    LANGSMITH_PROJECT: daiv-production
    LANGSMITH_API_KEY: <langsmith-api-key>

    Replace <langsmith-api-key> with your LangSmith API key.

  4. Recreate the services so they read the variables. On Docker Compose, run:

    Bash
    docker compose up -d

    On Docker Swarm, run:

    Bash
    docker stack deploy -c stack.yml daiv

  5. Start a run, for example a chat in the dashboard. A trace appears in your LangSmith project.

docs.title: Trace tags and metadata
docs.text:
Every agent run carries tags and metadata that you can filter and group by in LangSmith. The title and commit message generation run has its own, described below.

An agent run has these tags:

Tag Description Example Git platform The platform of the repository gitlab, github Repository slug The repository the run targets group/project Scope The conversation scope Issue, Merge Request, Global Agent name The agent that ran DAIV Agent

The scope tag is absent when the run has no scope. A run on a labelled GitLab issue carries gitlab, group/project, Issue and DAIV Agent.

Its metadata holds these fields:

Field Type Description repository string Repository slug, for example group/project git_platform string gitlab or github scope string Issue, Merge Request or Global trigger string What started the run: label, mention, job, chat or diff_to_metadata model string Primary model of the run, as a full model spec such as openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 thinking_level string Thinking level of the run; absent when the run has none lc_agent_name string The agent name, DAIV Agent author string User who created the issue or merge request (issue and merge request runs) triggered_by string User who triggered the run, who differs from the author on a mention (issue and merge request runs) issue_id int Issue IID (issue runs) labels list The issue's labels, lowercased (issue runs) merge_request_id int Merge request ID (merge request runs) ref string The branch the run was asked to use (job runs) override_source string or null explicit when the request picked the model, otherwise null (job and chat runs)

A run on a labelled issue has trigger set to label, and a run started by an @daiv mention on an issue, or on a merge request no session owns, has it set to mention. A chat message that starts a run on an idle session has chat and the Global scope. Every run DAIV takes from a session's inbox has job and the Global scope, as do runs from the jobs API, a schedule or the MCP endpoint. The inbox holds pipeline watch fixes, chat messages queued while the session was busy, delegation resumes and leg follow-ups, and @daiv mentions on a merge request the session owns.

The pull request title and commit message generation runs as a separate run named and tagged DiffToMetadata, with trigger set to diff_to_metadata. It carries the git platform, repository and scope tags and no agent name tag. It nests under the agent trace when DAIV publishes at the end of a run, and stands alone when DAIV recovers a draft.

docs.title: Create the LangSmith dashboard
docs.text:
DAIV creates a LangSmith dashboard named DAIV Monitoring with 27 charts in 8 groups, built on the tags and metadata above. You need the LangSmith variables from Trace runs with LangSmith set in the container.

Warning

Recreating the dashboard with --recreate deletes the existing DAIV Monitoring dashboard, including any chart you added by hand. setup_langsmith_dashboard describes it.

  1. Run the command, with your project name:

    Bash
    docker compose exec app django-admin setup_langsmith_dashboard --project <project-name>

    Replace <project-name> with your LangSmith project.

  2. In LangSmith, open the DAIV Monitoring dashboard of your project.

After you upgrade DAIV, run the command with --recreate to add the charts the upgrade brings.

Group Charts What it tracks Overview Trace volume and error rate by scope, trigger breakdown Activity and reliability Latency Median and P99 latency by scope, latency by repository Response times Cost Total cost by scope, prompt against completion cost, token usage by repository, P99 cost per run by trigger Spend Platform Volume and error rate by git platform, top repositories by volume Platform and repository breakdown Tools Subagent usage, tool call volume, tool error rate, MCP server tool usage What the agent calls LLM Call count, latency, prompt against completion tokens Model calls Model Trace volume, latency, cost and error rate by model Per-model comparison DiffToMetadata Volume, latency, error rate Title and commit message generation

To compare models, group a chart by the model metadata field. To see who starts the runs, group by author or triggered_by.

docs.title: Usage and cost
docs.text:
DAIV records the token usage and an estimated cost for every agent run in its own database, without a LangSmith account.

DAIV counts the tokens of every model call in the run, including fallback models, models that tools call, and subagents, and prices each call on its own. For a call through OpenRouter, the cost is the charge OpenRouter reports, which depends on the provider it routed the call to. For any other call, DAIV estimates it from the model's list price in genai-prices. DAIV then totals the tokens and cost per model, and stores the totals on the run.

A run records:

Field Description input_tokens Input tokens across all model calls output_tokens Output tokens across all model calls total_tokens Input plus output tokens cost_usd The run's cost in US dollars usage_by_model The same figures per model, with the cache and reasoning token counts the provider reports

Two limits apply:

  • For a call DAIV prices from list prices, the cost is empty when genai-prices does not list the model, and a run's cost is empty when any of its calls has no price. The tokens are still recorded, and DAIV logs a warning naming the model.
  • A cost priced from list prices is an estimate. Your provider's bill can differ.

You see the figures in three places. A row in the sessions list shows the session's cost, the Spend section of a session's Overview shows what the session cost, and a run's downloaded Markdown result holds total_tokens and cost_usd in its front matter. Sessions describes the pages.

docs.title: Export session archives
docs.text:
DAIV writes a copy of each session's conversation to its database when each run ends. This session archive is the saved copy, not a session's Archived state. The copy outlives the checkpointer's time to live and LangSmith's retention, and you can export it for offline analysis.

Warning

An export holds full conversations and run prompts. Store the output directory as you would the repositories' contents, and delete it when you finish.

  1. Run export_session_archives with an output directory, and with --since and --repo to narrow the sessions. The command's page holds the commands that write the files inside the container, copy them to the host and remove them.
  2. Open <thread_id>.json for each session.

Each file holds the session's repository, origin and title, and its contexts in order, where a /clear closes one context and starts the next and closed_at says when. Each context holds its messages in LangChain's messages_to_dict format. The file also holds each run's status, model, tokens and cost. The archive holds the session's messages, not each model request: system prompts, tool schemas, summaries and subagent internals stay in LangSmith. When a session fails to export, the command logs and names it, writes the rest, then exits with an error.

docs.title: Log events
docs.text: DAIV writes these events to its logs. Alert on them or search for them to find a problem early.

docs.title: Archive events
docs.text:
The daiv.sessions logger reports archive trouble. Errors reach Sentry.

Level Message Meaning ERROR executor: failed to archive thread_id=… A run's end was not archived, and the traceback says why, a timeout included. The next run's archive catches up. ERROR Thread … holds N messages, fewer than its archived M; keeping the archive The live thread lost messages the archive holds. DAIV leaves the archive as it was. ERROR Failed to load archived context N of thread …; leaving it out An archive row no longer decodes, and the transcript shows without it. WARNING No session … to archive its thread under A thread has no session, so DAIV archives nothing. INFO Restored thread … from archived context N An expired thread was seeded from its archive before a run.

A context that exists but fails to restore fails the run with ArchiveRestoreError and is not logged as one of these events.

docs.title: Bash policy events
docs.text:
The daiv.tools logger writes a warning when the sandbox bash tool blocks a command, or cannot parse one and so blocks it.

Text Only
[bash] bash_policy_denied: command denied (id=<call_id>, reason=default_disallow, rule='git push', segment='git push origin main')
Text Only
[bash] bash_policy_parse_failed: command could not be parsed (id=<call_id>, reason='Parse error: ...')

Each record carries these fields:

Field Description event bash_policy_denied or bash_policy_parse_failed reason_category default_disallow, global_disallow or parse_failure matched_rule The rule that blocked the command, for example git push; on bash_policy_denied only denied_segment The part of the command that was blocked; on bash_policy_denied only tool_call_id The agent's tool call ID, which matches the tool call in the LangSmith trace

default_disallow is a built-in rule, and global_disallow is a rule you set in DAIV_SANDBOX_COMMAND_POLICY_DISALLOW. A spike in bash_policy_denied means the agent keeps attempting a blocked command.

docs.title: No traces appear in LangSmith
docs.text: Check that LANGSMITH_TRACING is true and that the API key is correct. Check that the containers can reach the LangSmith endpoint, and read the application logs for authentication errors.

docs.title: A trace is incomplete
docs.text: Check that the project name is the same in every service. On Docker Swarm, check that the secret holding the API key is mounted.

docs.title: Site configuration
docs.text: Site Configuration is the admin-only page where you change DAIV's runtime behavior without redeploying. It groups settings by area and stores them in the database. You pick agent models, turn agent tools on or off, register LLM providers and switch OAuth login on or off, unless an environment variable or Docker secret overrides the field.

docs.title: Open the configuration page
docs.text:
You need an account with the admin role. Members do not see Site Configuration, and a member who opens its address is denied access.

  1. Sign in as an admin.
  2. Open /dashboard/configuration/. DAIV redirects you to the first group, Agent, at /dashboard/configuration/agent/.
  3. Select a group. Each group is a page at /dashboard/configuration/<group_key>/, and an unknown key returns a 404.
  4. Change the fields, then select Save configuration. DAIV shows "Configuration saved."

Saving a group writes only that group's fields. A saved change takes effect immediately for the next read: the save commits in a transaction and clears the read cache when it commits. An agent run reads its settings once, when it starts, so a change applies from the next run. The read cache keeps a value for 5 minutes, which matters only for changes made outside this page, such as a direct database edit: they can take that long to appear.

docs.title: Setting groups
docs.text:
The configuration has the following groups, organized by category.

Group Category What it configures Agent AI tasks Primary, fallback and daiv-max models; their thinking levels; the agent recursion limit; the per-request LLM timeout and retry count (applied to every provider and model-backed task); whether to suggest a context file (e.g. AGENTS.md) on new merge requests; whether to link sessions from merge requests; and Subagent models, the model the general-purpose and explore subagents run on in every repository (see Subagents). An entry already stored for a skill or subagent that only repositories define is listed there too, so it can be changed or cleared. A skill's model, and those of the code-review detectors, are set on the skill's page in Skills (see Agent skills). Commit & PR Writer AI tasks Primary and fallback models that generate commit messages and pull/merge request descriptions from diffs. Titling AI tasks Primary and fallback models that generate session and run titles from prompts. Memory AI tasks Capture learnings from finished runs, consolidate them into a per-repository memory document, and inject them into future runs. The models that extract observations from each finished run's transcript and rewrite the memory document, the consolidation thresholds (minimum pending observations, maximum pending age, minimum interval), and the caps on the memory document's lines and bytes. Run classifier AI tasks Primary and fallback models that classify each finished scheduled run's report into an envelope. Providers Models LLM provider records (slug, wire protocol, base URL, API key, extra headers and more) that every model field draws from. See Providers. Web Search Agent tools Turn the web search tool on or off, pick DuckDuckGo, Tavily or SearXNG, set the maximum results, store the Tavily API key, and set the SearXNG search URL and timeout. See Set up SearXNG. Web Fetch Agent tools Turn the web fetch tool on or off, choose the model that processes fetched pages, set the cache TTL, timeout and maximum content size, and define per-domain auth headers. Sandbox Runtime Sandbox request timeout and the sandbox API key. Jobs Runtime Per-user rate limit for Jobs API submissions (e.g. 20/hour). Pipeline Watch Runtime Watch CI on merge requests DAIV publishes and try to fix failures, and how many fix attempts (at least 1) to spend on one merge request before handing back. Rocket Chat Integrations Offer Rocket.Chat as a notification channel, with the instance URL, bot user ID and auth token. Telegram Integrations Offer Telegram as a notification channel, with the bot token from @BotFather. See Set up Telegram. Authentication Integrations OAuth login with your Git platform: the login toggle, open signup, the OAuth client ID and secret and, for GitLab, the instance URLs. See Turn on OAuth login.

docs.title: How environment variables and the UI interact
docs.text:
Each configurable field resolves through three tiers, highest first:

  1. Environment variable or Docker secret. When set, the matching field is locked: the page shows a "Locked by environment variable" tooltip and you cannot edit the field.
  2. Database value. The value you save here, when it is not empty.
  3. Built-in default. The value DAIV ships with.

A value you save here takes effect only if no environment variable overrides it. If you leave a field blank, DAIV falls back to the environment variable, if any, and then to the built-in default. To keep a field editable, leave its variable unset rather than set to an empty value: an empty variable still locks the field.

The environment variable for a field is DAIV_<FIELD_NAME>; for example, agent_recursion_limit maps to DAIV_AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT. The Authentication fields are the exception and map to the ALLAUTH_* variables:

Field Environment variable OAuth client ID ALLAUTH_CLIENT_ID Auth Client Secret ALLAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET GitLab URL ALLAUTH_GITLAB_URL GitLab server URL ALLAUTH_GITLAB_SERVER_URL

Environment variables lists every variable with its default, and marks the ones that are env-only.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: DAIV stores the secret fields on this page encrypted in the database: the Web Search API key, Sandbox API key, Auth Client Secret, Rocketchat Auth Token, Telegram Bot Token, each provider's API key and the per-domain web fetch header values. External URL and encryption key lists everything DAIV encrypts. The page never shows a stored secret again: it shows a masked hint. Leave a secret field blank to keep the stored value, or select Clear to remove it. The key comes from DAIV_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
The Providers group holds the LLM providers DAIV can call. Every model field in the other groups draws its models from the providers you enable here, and a model is written as <slug>:<model-name>; LLM providers explains how a model spec picks its provider.

DAIV creates four built-in providers the first time it runs: anthropic, openai, google_genai and openrouter, listed under Built-in. Their slug and provider type are locked, and you cannot delete them, but you can set their API keys and base URLs and turn them on or off. A built-in provider whose key was not seeded starts disabled; see the LLM provider variables for how the keys are seeded. You add any other provider under Custom, for example a vLLM, llama.cpp or LiteLLM server or an internal gateway.

docs.title: Provider fields
docs.text:
Field Description Slug The prefix of <slug>:<model-name>. It starts with a lowercase letter, holds lowercase letters, digits, - and _, and has at most 32 characters. google is reserved. It cannot change after creation: delete the provider and add it again to change it. Display name The name shown in the list. It has at most 64 characters. Provider type The wire protocol: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenRouter. Base URL The endpoint to call instead of the provider's default, with an http or https scheme. For an OpenAI-typed server, include the version segment, for example /v1: DAIV warns when it is missing, because requests would reach the wrong route. API key The credential for the endpoint, stored encrypted. Extra headers (JSON) A JSON object of additional request headers, for example {"X-Foo": "bar"}. Header values must be strings. Headers the agent manages itself take precedence. Enabled Whether models can use the provider. Enabling a provider needs an API key. Use Responses API Applies to OpenAI-typed providers only. Turn it on for servers that expose /v1/responses, and leave it off for servers that offer only /v1/chat/completions, such as most vLLM, llama.cpp and LiteLLM setups. Verify TLS certificates On by default. Applies to OpenAI- and OpenRouter-typed providers only: for the others, DAIV warns that turning it off has no effect.

A model field anywhere in the configuration is rejected on save when its provider is disabled or has no API key, with a message that points you to the Providers group.

docs.title: Add a custom provider
docs.text:
Add a provider to use models from a server other than the four built-in providers. You need the admin role, the endpoint's URL and its API key.

  1. In Configuration → Providers, select Add custom provider.
  2. In Slug, enter the model prefix.
  3. In Display name, enter the name to show in the list.
  4. In Provider type, choose the wire protocol the server speaks.
  5. In Base URL, enter the endpoint's URL.
  6. In API key, enter the key.
  7. Select Save configuration.
  8. Use <slug>:<model-name> wherever a model is specified, with <slug> replaced by the slug and <model-name> by a model the endpoint serves.

Warning

Turn off Verify TLS certificates only for self-hosted endpoints behind an internal or self-signed CA. Without verification, the connection is open to man-in-the-middle attacks. Mount the CA certificate into the DAIV containers instead when you can.

docs.title: Set up SearXNG
docs.text:
Warning

SearXNG forwards queries to its upstream search engines. Self-hosting does not keep the query text local, and a query can contain repository code or other private information.

By default, web search uses DuckDuckGo. To send the agent's searches to a SearXNG instance instead, you need:

  • A SearXNG instance that the DAIV app and workers can reach without authentication, and that allows JSON responses: json is in search.formats of its settings, for example [html, json].

  • The complete search endpoint, for example https://search.example.com/search, or https://search.example.com/searxng/search when SearXNG runs under a prefix. It must use http or https and hold no credentials, query string or fragment.

  • In Configuration → Web Search, set Web search engine to SearXNG.

  • Enter the endpoint in SearXNG search URL.
  • Optionally, set SearXNG request timeout, from 1 to 120 seconds. The default is 15 seconds.
  • Select Save configuration.

Leave the Tavily API key as it is: SearXNG does not use it. The existing maximum results and web search switch apply to SearXNG too. To configure it from the environment instead, set DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE, DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_URL and DAIV_WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; see Web search.

DAIV sends a GET request with q and format=json and does not follow redirects, so enter the final endpoint. Chat, GitLab and GitHub runs and other agent entry points share the web search tool, and the model decides when to call it. DAIV itself makes the request, so it does not need an opening in a sandbox environment's egress policy. DAIV keeps HTTPS certificate verification on. A failed search reaches the agent as a tool failure, not as an empty result.

docs.title: Allow DAIV through the SearXNG limiter
docs.text:
DAIV sends Accept-Language: en, which SearXNG's header checks expect. If the SearXNG limiter (server.limiter) is on, it can still answer automated requests with HTTP 429. To exempt DAIV, add its source address to /etc/searxng/limiter.toml:

TOML
[botdetection.ip_lists]
pass_ip = ["192.0.2.10"]

Replace 192.0.2.10 with the address SearXNG sees for the DAIV app and workers, or with a narrow trusted subnet. The list exempts those clients from bot detection, so keep it narrow rather than turning the limiter off. For pass lists and reverse-proxy client addresses, see the SearXNG limiter documentation. For the JSON format setting and the endpoint contract, see the SearXNG Search API.

docs.title: Turn on OAuth login
docs.text:
OAuth login lets users sign in with their Git platform account. You need an OAuth app on that platform: see Create the OAuth app.

  1. In Configuration, open Authentication.
  2. Turn on the toggle next to the group title. It is the Enable OAuth login setting, and DAIV hides the group's other fields while it is off.
  3. Enter the OAuth client ID and the Auth Client Secret. Enter both: DAIV rejects a save that sets only one.
  4. On GitLab, set GitLab URL to the address your users' browsers open. If DAIV reaches GitLab at a different address, such as one inside a Docker network, set GitLab server URL to it. GitHub installs do not show these two fields.
  5. Optionally, turn on Open social signup to let anyone who authenticates through the Git platform create an account. When it is off, only users an admin created can sign in.
  6. Select Save configuration.

The CODEBASE_CLIENT setting decides which fields the group shows and which provider DAIV offers. DAIV creates no accounts through standard email signup, which is off.

docs.title: Set up Telegram
docs.text:
You need a bot token from @BotFather, and a DAIV_EXTERNAL_URL that Telegram can reach.

Warning

Give each DAIV instance its own bot. Telegram allows one webhook per bot, so if a second instance uses the same token, the webhook moves to it and the first instance stops receiving Telegram's updates, including the connect handshake. DAIV's reconcile job logs the URL it finds but cannot prevent this.

  1. In Configuration → Telegram, turn on the toggle next to the group title. It is the Enable Telegram setting, and DAIV hides the group's other fields while it is off.
  2. Enter the token in Telegram Bot Token.
  3. Select Save configuration.

DAIV checks a typed token with Telegram when you save. It rejects a token Telegram refuses, and saves a token it could not check because Telegram was unreachable, with a warning, so an outage does not block an unrelated edit. The group then shows the bot username. Users connect their account from the notification channels page; see Notifications.

docs.title: Telegram derived values
docs.text:
You type only the bot token. DAIV derives the rest:

  • Bot username. DAIV reads it from Telegram with getMe when you save the group, and again in a reconcile job that runs every 15 minutes. The page shows it read-only, because a hand-typed username that disagrees with the token breaks the connect link without any visible error. An empty value means the derivation has not run yet.
  • Webhook secret. DAIV generates it, stores it encrypted and sends it to Telegram when it registers the webhook. You never see it or type it. The webhook rejects every update until the secret exists, so a blank value means the sync has not finished.

Saving is not the only trigger: the reconcile job compares the webhook Telegram has registered with the desired URL and registers it again when they differ. That brings an instance configured only through DAIV_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and DAIV_TELEGRAM_ENABLED, which may never open this page, into line, and it recovers a webhook that Telegram disabled after repeated failures.

Turning Telegram off keeps the stored webhook secret. If you turn it off with no bot token available, because you cleared it or never set it while a webhook was registered, DAIV cannot remove the webhook and shows a warning: remove it in BotFather, or restore the token and turn the channel off again. A group that never had a webhook registered saves without a warning.
